# Ocular

> Ocular gives AI agents real eyes on your dev server and the live web — one MCP connection, $2.50 a month. No infrastructure to run, no blocks to fight. Read-only: Ocular cannot act on your browser.

Ocular is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives AI agents web vision, over two execution paths: a local worker for localhost and your own dev server (unmetered, renders on your machine), and a cloud worker for the public web (stealth-hardened, quota-capped). Five tools, one MCP connection — your agent doesn't need to know which path served a given request.

- [Homepage](https://www.useocular.dev) — positioning, pricing, and FAQ.
- [Pricing](https://www.useocular.dev/#pricing) — $2.50/month: unlimited local captures, plus 40 cloud renders/day.

## Tools

- `view_page` — full-page or viewport screenshot of any URL, at low/balanced/high detail.
- `inspect_ui` — derived design tokens (palette, typography, spacing, breakpoints) for a page, without raw CSS.
- `extract_assets` — inline SVGs and image URLs, rewritten to absolute, safe-to-fetch links.
- `motion_capture` — animations and scroll effects captured as discrete stills (no video, no animated GIF).
- `get_quota` — remaining cloud renders and reset time for the connected account. Local captures are unmetered and don't draw from this.

## Pricing

$2.50/month: unlimited renders of localhost and your own dev server, plus 40 public-web renders/day. On the cloud path, full charge only on a successful render; half charge if the stealth ladder exhausts every escalation and still fails; nothing charged on a render error. Local captures never touch quota or billing.

## Security

Ocular is read-only — it cannot click, type, fill forms, or navigate with side effects; it cannot act on your browser. This removes action risk, not content risk: captured page content still enters the calling agent's context, the same as any other tool that reads the web. Authenticated/cookie-based browsing is planned for the local path only, via a browser profile you log into once on your own machine — that session never leaves your device. It is not, and will not be, supported on the public-web path.
